headline: Solar boom powers ahead in Trump-voting states
meta_description: More than 70% of new US solar power is being built in states that voted Trump in 2024, with eight of the top 10 solar states backing him.
summary_short: A surprising shift: the majority of America's new solar installations are happening in states that voted for Trump, signaling bipartisan momentum for clean energy.
body:
More than 70% of new US solar power is being built in states that voted for Trump in 2024. Eight of the country's top 10 solar-building states backed him in the election.

The US added more than 11 gigawatts of solar capacity, yet this expansion is concentrated in politically conservative regions. The data reveals a quiet consensus: renewable energy development transcends partisan lines, driven by economics, local job creation, and falling technology costs.

The story challenges common assumptions about clean energy as a strictly progressive cause. In Trump-voting states, solar projects attract investment and employment regardless of national political alignment, suggesting that energy transitions may ultimately succeed when they serve local community interests.
quick_facts: Over 70% of new US solar power built in Trump-voting states
Eight of top 10 solar-building states voted Trump in 2024
US added more than 11 GW of solar capacity
